title: Why Warm Seas Hold Less
question: Why does a warming ocean lose oxygen?
hook: The oceans have already lost 1-2% of their oxygen, and rising water temperature is a big part of the reason.
idea: Warmer water dissolves less oxygen and mixes less with deeper water, so less oxygen reaches the depths while sea life keeps using it.

beats.prompt: The top layer of the sea warms by a few degrees. What happens to the oxygen supply reaching deeper water?

choices.label: It rises, because warm water sinks and carries oxygen down
choices.feedback: Warm water is more buoyant, so it tends to stay on top rather than sink.

choices.label: It stays the same, since temperature doesn't affect oxygen
choices.feedback: Temperature changes both how much oxygen dissolves and how much the layers mix.

choices.label: It falls, because warm buoyant water mixes less with the water below

beats.explain: Warmer water is more buoyant and holds less oxygen, so less oxygenated surface water mixes down into deeper water.

beats.prompt: Sort each into whether it supplies oxygen to the sea or cuts the supply.
beats.explain: Oxygen comes in at the surface from the air and phytoplankton, while stratification and lower solubility in warm, salty water reduce the supply.

beats.prompt: Match each part of the ocean to the kind of oxygen loss it shows.
pairs: Lower oxygen solubility as it warms
beats.explain: Coastal waters lose oxygen through eutrophication, the open ocean's natural low-oxygen zones are spreading, and warming cuts how much oxygen the upper ocean holds.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Oxygen enters the sea at the surface
Living things use oxygen at every depth
Warming strengthens layering, so less surface water mixes downward
So warming increases the oxygen supply to deep water
beats.explain: Stronger stratification reduces the supply of oxygen from the surface, so warming makes deep oxygen loss worse, not better.
